prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1074; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss came in describing a left-turn collision at an intersection. The insured driver is named on the policy, and nothing suggests the coverage period had lapsed or that the damage predates it.

Entry 2: Scene photographs show front-quarter and passenger-side damage that is largely in line with the impact as described. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection history.

Entry 3: Claimant reports a wrist fracture, and the injury fits the kind and force expected from this type of crash. No earlier injury to the same area is on record. The claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far.

Entry 4: The responding officer and the other parties on scene state that the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash occurred. No independent witnesses have come forward, and the photographs confirm some details but not the claimant's position at impact.

Entry 5: Claimant is now represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney. Treatment has followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved, according to the records received so far.

Entry 6: File reviewed. Vehicle damage and injury are both broadly consistent with the reported impact. Open items are the claimant's position at impact and counsel's written response. Reserve maintained pending that review.
